name: Shopify
tagline: Hosted ecommerce platform for stores, payments, checkout, and operations

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked; regional page showed US$25 annual-effective while US public references commonly list Basic $39/month monthly and $29/month annually.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Simple online store and product links; 0 staff accounts; 5% transaction fee with Shopify Payments.
tiers.notes: Only available to new merchants and stores still in the free-trial period; no annual price is published.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited products; 10 inventory locations; 0 additional staff accounts; 2% fee when using a third-party payment provider.

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.limits: Unlimited products; 10 inventory locations; up to 5 staff accounts; 1% third-party-provider fee.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: Unlimited products; 10 inventory locations; up to 15 staff accounts; 0.6% third-party-provider fee.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Starts at $2,300/month; unlimited staff; up to 200 inventory locations, 9 expansion stores and 20 POS Pro locations; 0.2% third-party-provider fee.
tiers.notes: Starting price typically requires a 1- or 3-year contract; exact quote varies.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 3-day trial, then a promotional $1/month for 3 months before standard pricing
pricing.billingTerms: Starter is monthly only; Basic/Grow/Advanced offer monthly + annual; Plus uses 1- or 3-year contracts
pricing.hiddenCosts: Starter charges a 5% transaction fee with Shopify Payments; POS Pro is $89/month per location on non-Plus plans; synced marketplace orders above 50/month cost 1% up to $99/month; third-party gateway fees (2%/1%/0.6%/0.2%) are on top of the provider's processing fees; apps, themes and domains can add recurring costs.

verdictSummary: You can build a small store, but Shopify's product is hosted checkout, payments, tax/shipping integrations, app marketplace, fraud/risk tooling, and merchant operations.
coreLoopDIY: For a tiny shop, build catalog/cart/checkout via Stripe, order emails, and simple admin; do not expect Shopify parity.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because ecommerce failures cost real revenue and trust.

priorArt.name: Medusa
priorArt.desc: Open-source commerce platform for custom stores; substantial prior art but not Shopify's h

alternatives.name: Bagisto
alternatives.desc: A proper Laravel storefront and admin; the free bit ends where hosting and Laravel operations begin.

facts.install: Install with Composer/Git and run php artisan bagisto:install, or use the supplied Docker route
facts.dataFormat: Catalog, customers and orders in a MySQL-compatible database; media and generated assets in Laravel's server storage/public directories
facts.gapVsPaid: Bagisto lacks Shopify's managed checkout, hosting, app ecosystem, multichannel operations and support; Laravel operations become the merchant's job.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a Laravel stack: compatible PHP, Composer, Node build tools, database and web-server configuration

alternatives.name: Magento Open Source
alternatives.desc: A vast store engine for anyone who thought running WooCommerce did not involve enough infrastructure.

alternatives.name: OpenCart
alternatives.desc: Old-school PHP commerce that still does the whole job instead of selling you ten add-ons first.

facts.install: Upload a stable PHP release to hosting, create a database, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Catalog, customers and orders in a SQL database; images, downloads and application storage in server directories
facts.gapVsPaid: OpenCart's themes, admin, integrations and multichannel operations are much less refined, and the merchant owns the server.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, database and permissions work come first, followed by payment, shipping, mail and extension configuration

alternatives.name: Shopware Community Edition
alternatives.desc: A serious modern store; free licence, expensive appetite for RAM and competent administration.

facts.install: Use Shopware's official Docker/CLI setup or its web installer on a supported server
facts.dataFormat: Commerce records in a MySQL-compatible database; media and cache on the filesystem or configured S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Shopware Community Edition demands far more infrastructure and administration and has a smaller plug-and-play ecosystem than Shopify.
facts.setupBlocker: The Docker route asks for roughly 8 GB minimum and 16 GB recommended RAM, plus competent server administration

alternatives.name: Vvveb
alternatives.desc: A visual CMS and complete shop in one PHP install; obscure, capable and still your server.

facts.install: Download and upload the PHP release, open the site URL, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Content, products, orders and settings in MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite or PostgreSQL; media and downloadable files on the server filesystem
facts.gapVsPaid: Vvveb cannot match Shopify's app ecosystem, multichannel operations, managed checkout reliability or support.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable files, mail and payment configuration, plus ongoing server updates

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Popular answer, wrong audience: a headless commerce development platform, not a store a non-builder installs.

rejectedAlternatives.name: nopCommerce
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Calls itself open source, but its custom NPL is not OSI-approved and requires a powered-by link on every interface screen.

notes: A valuable no: the app is not just product pages and a cart.
prompt:
Build me a small self-hosted shop for a handful of products, the honest small
slice of Shopify. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on a VPS; products in products.json (slug,
  name, price, images, stock count), server-rendered catalog and product pages.
- Cart in a session cookie; checkout hands off entirely to Stripe Checkout
  (keys in .env). Never touch card data.
- Stripe webhook records the order, decrements stock, and emails me and the
  buyer via Resend (key in .env).
- An /admin page behind basic auth: order list and a mark-shipped button that
  emails the buyer with an optional tracking number.
- Flat shipping rates per region in a config file; sold-out products stay
  visible but cannot be bought.
- No customer accounts, no telemetry; orders stay in my SQLite file.
- Out of scope: discount engines, multi-currency, POS, and tax automation. Use
  Stripe Tax for tax; do not write tax logic.
- README: Stripe webhook setup, a plain warning that I am now the fraud
  department, and a note that this is not Shopify, whose trusted checkout,
  payment risk handling, and app ecosystem cannot be rebuilt; if volume grows,
  move to Shopify or Medusa rather than growing this.
